levels.formal: For a gauge group with a $U(1)$ factor acting on left-handed Weyl fermions, with the $U(1)$ charges $Y$, the four anomaly-cancellation conditions are: $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$, the sum of $Y$ over the colour triplets and antitriplets (each weighted by its $SU(2)$ multiplicity) vanishes; $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$, the sum of $Y$ over the weak doublets (each weighted by its colour multiplicity) vanishes; $U(1)^{3}$, the sum of $Y^{3}$ over all Weyl fermions vanishes; and mixed gravitational, the sum of $Y$ over all Weyl fermions vanishes. A right-handed Weyl fermion of charge $Y$ enters the conditions as a left-handed one of charge $-Y$ in the conjugate representation. The four conditions are necessary for the consistency of the gauge theory, and a failure of any of them is not lifted by spontaneous breaking: an anomalous $U(1)$ cannot be gauged whether or not it is broken. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[\S 22.4]{WeinbergQFT2}.
levels.technical:
For left-handed Weyl fermions with $U(1)$ charges $Y$, consistency of the gauge theory requires four sums to vanish: $\sum Y$ over colour triplets and antitriplets, weighted by $SU(2)$ multiplicity, for $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$; $\sum Y$ over weak doublets, weighted by colour multiplicity, for $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$; $\sum Y^{3}$ over all Weyl fermions for $U(1)^{3}$; and $\sum Y$ over all Weyl fermions for the mixed gravitational anomaly.

A right-handed fermion of charge $Y$ enters as a left-handed one of charge $-Y$ in the conjugate representation. The conditions are necessary, and spontaneous breaking does not rescue an anomalous $U(1)$. The result is imported from the standard quantum field theory literature.
levels.lay: A gauge theory with chiral fermions only makes sense quantum mechanically if certain sums of the charges cancel. For a theory with a $U(1)$ factor alongside the colour and weak forces there are four such sums. If any one of them fails the theory is inconsistent, and breaking the symmetry does not repair it. This is a standard textbook result taken from the literature.
levels.one-liner: A $U(1)$ gauge factor acting on Weyl fermions is consistent only if four anomaly sums vanish: the two mixed with $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$, the cubic one and the gravitational one.
